name: showreel-t02-php2shell

voice.text: Attackers have started trying [PHP2Shell](/pˌiˌeɪʧpˈi tə ʃˈɛl/). It lets anyone run code on a PHP server, no login needed. Check your PHP version. Below the fixed release on screen? Then you're exposed. Update today, and the attempts bounce off.

caption:
Attackers have started trying PHP2Shell. 🚨

The two critical PHP flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) let someone run code on a PHP server without logging in. Security firms report exploit attempts hitting the internet since the patches landed; the UK's NCSC had not confirmed successful attacks yet. The fixes shipped 21–22 Oct: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Run php -v, and if you're below your branch's fix, update today.
Send this to whoever runs your website.

sources.note: PHP's own changelog: 8.4.27 (22 Oct 2026) fixes CVE-2026-109618/-109619; same entry in 8.5.12, 8.3.36, 8.2.35
CISA alert, unauthenticated remote code execution
news: first exploitation attempts seen by watchTowr; NCSC had no confirmed exploitation (Techzine)
